GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4250 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
RAISING OF GUARANTEED WORKING DAYS UNDER MGNREGS 
 
4250.  ADV. DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has the data of fund allocated and spending pattern of 
activities carried out under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme (MGNREGS) and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government will consider the proposal to raise guaranteed working days 
to 150 days from the current 100 days and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government has received any request/representation showing the lack of 
timely payment of wages due to Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe workers under the 
MGNREGS and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
(d)  whether the Government has taken any action based on such complaints from the 
State of Kerala and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a):     Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment programme. Hence, no State/UT -wise 
financial allocation is made under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS.  
  
During the current financial year 20 21-22 (as on 25.03.2022), an amount of Rs. 
91,855.65 crore has been released by Central Government to the States/UTs under Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS. 
  
(b):    Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGA) is to provide at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year 
to each household in rural areas of the country whose adult members volunteers to do 
unskilled manual work. In addition to this, there is a provision for upto additional 50 days per 
household of un skilled wage employment in a financial year in drought/natural calamity 
affected notified rural areas. As per Section 3 (4) of Act, the State Governments may make 
provision for providing additional days   beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from 
their own funds.   
  
(c)&(d):       The category wise (SC, ST and Others) wage payment system, as made 
applicable from the financial year 2021 -22, has been introduced to accurately reflect the on -
ground flow of funds to various population group. Its further st reamlining is being 
undertaken.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4253 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
DISHA COMMITTEE 
 
4253.  SHRI SANJAY SETH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the targets fixed for the DISHA Committee and the objectives of its establishment 
along with minimum period of interval to organise its meetings; 
(b)  the number of meetings of DISHA held in various districts of Jharkhand and the 
schemes discussed in these meetings along with the status of the same during the last 
three years; 
(c)  the number of schemes being run for development of rural areas by the Ministry and 
the number of schemes functional in Jharkhand; and 
(d)  the total amount of funds released for these schemes during the last two years, 
scheme-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)      District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee (DISHA) are 
constituted at State and District levels to monitor the implementation of various schemes of 
the Central Government and ensure coordination among all stakeholders, including elected 
representatives and concerned officials for efficient and time -bound development of dist ricts 
in the country.  As per the DISHA Guidelines, the State level DISHA Committee meeting 
should be held at least once in every six months and the District level DISHA Committee 
meeting should be held at least once in every quarter. 
(b)     The details of  number of meetings of DISHA held in various districts of Jharkhand 
during the last three years as well as the schemes discussed in these meetings are provided in 
Annexure-I. The schemes discussed in the meetings are currently operational in the State of 
Jharkhand. 
(c) & (d) The details of schemes being run by the Ministry of Rural Development for 
development of rural areas and functional in Jharkhand along with the funds released to the 
State under these schemes during the last two years are enclosed in Annexure -II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4254 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
BENEFICIARIES OF GKRA 
 
4254.  SHRI GAJANAN KIRTIKAR: 
SHRI C.N. ANNADURAI: 
SHRI SELVAM G.: 
SHRI GAUTHAM SIGAMANI PON: 
SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH alias PAWAN RAJENIMBALKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has achieved the objective for which Garib Kalyan Rojgar 
Abhiyaan (GKRA) was launched and if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
(b)  the details of the total number of beneficiaries of the GKRA and the number of 
migrant labourers trained, State/UT-wise including Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; 
(c)  the number of districts in different States covered under GKRA; 
(d)  the number of mandays generated so far under GKRA; 
(e)  whether any skill based training programme was also conducted under GKRA and if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  the other steps taken by the Government to promote skilling and entrepreneurship for 
rural development? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (d)  The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) was launched on 20th June 2020, for 
a period of 125 days, with resource envelop of Rs. 50,000 Crore to boost employment and 
livelihood opportunities for migrant workers returning to villages and similarly affected 
citizens in rural area. The Abhiyaan adopted a multipronged strategy of providing immediate 
employment & livelihood opportunities to the distressed, to saturate the villages with public 
infrastructure and creation of livelihood assets to boost the income g eneration activities and 
enhance long term livelihood opportunities by giving focus on 25 works (including works 
under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme) in 116 selected 
districts across 6 States namely Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Prad esh, Odisha, Rajasthan 
and Uttar Pradesh.  The GKRA ended on 22nd October, 2020  and a total of 50.78 crore 
person-days employment were generated with a total expenditure of Rs. 39,293 crore during 
the Abhiyaan. 
No districts of Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu were included in the Garib Kalyan Rojgar 
Abhiyaan. The details of physical achievements/work done during the Garib Kalyan Rojgar 
Abhiyaan is given at Annexure.  
  
 
 

State-wise number of districts covered under the Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan is given as 
below: 
  
Sr. No. State Number of Districts 
1 Bihar 32 
2 Jharkhand 3 
3 Madhya Pradesh 24 
4 Odisha 4 
5 Rajasthan 22 
6 Uttar Pradesh 31 
Total  116 
  
    
(e)      Training has been conducted through Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) during Garib 
Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan. A total of 1,922 trainings were conducted and 68,136 candidates 
were trained. 
(f)      There are two skill development programme for rural youth under DAY -NRLM, 
namely, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY) and Rural Self 
Employment Training institutes (RSETIs). Both these programmes are aimed at increasing 
employability of rural youth, either for wage employment or self employment. 
                  
 Project ‘UNNATI’, launched in December 2019 by Government of India, is a skilling project 
that intends to upgrade the skill base of the Mahatma Gandhi NREGS workers, and thereby 
improve their livelihoods, so that they can move from the current partial employment to full 
employment.  
  
The Ministry of Rural Development has launched the Rural Mason Training (RMT) program 
under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY -G) to address the issue of 
insufficient number of skilled masons for construction of quality PMAY -G houses. The 
initiative not only avails livelihood opportunities f or the rural workforce but also contributes 
towards the availability of a skilled workforce for the construction of rural infrastructure 
under different schemes. The MoRD has partnered with the Construction Skill Development 
Council of India (CSDCI) and Na tional Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in the 
implementation of the RMT program. 
  
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is implementing Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) under Skill India Mission for skill based training of the  
youth across the country   (including youth belonging to rural areas) under Short Term 
Training (STT) courses and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). Under PMKVY, STT is 
linked to placement, while RPL does not mandate placements as it recognizes the exist ing 
skills of candidate.  
  
At present, third phase of PMKVY i.e. PMKVY 3.0 is being implemented. PMKVY 3.0 is a 
demand driven scheme with bottom -up approach and District Skill Committees (DSCs) have 
been entrusted with the task of identifying local demand , based on which training has been 
arranged in the district which strengthens the local skill capability including in the rural areas. 
Also, Skill Hub Initiative has been launched under the PMKVY 3.0 wherein the focus is on 
the introduction of skill traini ng programmes in the education ecosystems. The initiative 
would consider the policy level synergy on integration of vocational education with general 
education as envisioned in the NEP 2020. 
  
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4255 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29th MARCH 2022 
 
AUSTRALIAN DAIRY MAJORS 
4255. SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B.: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government had entered into an agreement with Australia by 
which the Government intends to allow Australian dairy ma jors to enter into country’s dairy 
sector; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also true that farmers and their unions have strongly opposed such move; and 
(d) whether it is a fact that many farmers in the country who do not have land were depending on 
the dairy sector and therefore, allowing such majors into dairy sector will make their life 
miserable? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a)  No agreement with Australia to allow Australian dairy majors to enter into country’s dairy 
sector has been signed. 
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above. 
(c) Yes Sir. 
(d) Does not arise in view of (a) above.

4261.  SHRI D.K. SURESH: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to  establish sports schools in 
every district in the country; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the number of such  schools established so 
far, State/UT-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has re ceived any proposal from various States

{ SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR } 
 
(a) to (d) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility of establishing 
sports schools in the country rests primarily with the State / Union Territory

Further, it may be informed that 247 sports academies have been 
accreditated under the Khelo India Scheme across the country, including 27 
in the State of Karna taka, on the basis of proposals received through the 
State/UT Governments.

4262. SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR(ALIAS) VIJAY VASANTH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी  मंत्री be pleased to state:  
 
 
(a) the names of places in the country where fishing harbours are located along with their estimated handling 
capacity, State-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has any proposal to modernize some of the fishing harbours; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof and the amount allocated for the purpose, State-wise including Tamil Nadu;  
(d) whether it is also proposed to set up integrated seaweed parks in Tamil Nadu; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with estimated cost including proposed functions thereof and the time by 
which these are likely to be set up? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) to (c) : The name of places in the Country where fishing harbours /landing centres are located is at 
Annexure-I. It is to state that the handling capacity of such structures will vary depending on the size and type 
of vessel s, frequency of arrival, available work force and machinery etc . The Department of Fisheries, 
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  has been implementing a flagship scheme namely 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a highest-ever investment of Rs. 20,050 crore in all 
States/Union Territories (UTs) including in the State of Tamil Nadu for development of fisheries with effect 
from financial year 2020 -21. Development of fishing harbours and fish landing centres is one of the thrust 
areas under PMMSY and an investment of about Rs.3500 crore has been envisaged for this purpose. Under 
PMMSY, central financial assistance upto 60% of project cost for the States and upto 100% for the UTs is 
provided for the development of fishing harbours and fish landing centres.  Further the entire cost for 
modernization of fishing harbours exclusively owned by the Central Government and its entities  are borne by 
the Gov ernment of India . PMMSY also envisages suitable linkages and convergence with the Sagarmala 
Scheme of Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways  (MoPSW) for development of fishing harbours/fish 
landing centres.  

Page 2 of 8 
 
 
The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during 202 1-22 
has  accorded approval to  four fishing harbour proposals under PMMSY in a convergence mode of 
implementation by sharing the central financial liability equally between the PMMSY of DoF and Sagarmala 
of MoPSW. Details of the same are placed at Annexure-II. In addition, 14 Fishing Harbours  of various 
States/UTs including Tamil Nadu  have been approved for development/upgradation under the Fisheries and 
Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) in which interest subvention is provided by Government 
of India for the loans to be taken by State G overnments to finance the projects.  Details of the same are 
provided at Annexure-III.   
  
(d) to (e): A Concept Note relating to  establishment of Multipurpose Seaweed Park has been received from the 
State Government of Tamil Nadu, at an estimated cost of Rs.296.43 crores under the PMMSY to be established 
in a hub and spoke model. The project aims to enhance the production of seaweed and to create viable 
alternative livelihood options for the coastal  communities by introducing them to seaweed cultivation. 
However, a detailed project report along with firmed up cost with necessary approvals is yet to be received.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
DIFFICULTIES FACED BY MGNREGS LABOURERS 
 
4263.  SHRI DEEPAK BAIJ: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether any study has been conducted to know the difficulties being faced by the 
labourers in the online payment of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) in Naxalite areas; 
(b)  whether the Government is contemplating to pay-in-cash under MGNREGS in 
Naxalites areas of Bastar division where bank branches are very few or far away; 
(c)  the details of the difficulties being faced by the MGNREGS labourers to get payment 
from the Bank; and 
(d)  whether any study has been conducted by the Ministry thereon and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)to(d):       Under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), wage payment is made directly into the accounts of the 
beneficiaries  through National electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) as per DBT 
protocol. 
 
          As per the request of States/UTs exemption has been provided to release the payment 
either through e -FMS (currently for State of Manipur, UT of Dadara and Nagar Haveli and 
Daman and Diu, Andman & Nicobar) or cash payment in the selected areas of the 
States/UTs.  
 
          Currently in four Integrated Action Plan (IAP)  districts of Bastar division  of 
Chhattisgarh in Naxalite affected area namely, Bijapur, Dantewada, Narayanpur and 
Sukma, wage payment is released through cash for selected Gram Panchyats as per the 
request of State. Similarly, for unbanked areas of State of Manipur, in 34 blocks, wage 
payment is made through cash/cheque as per the request of State. At present 99.7 percent 
wage payment under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS  is made through e-transfer.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4266 
ANSWERED ON 29.03.2022 
 
HINDUSTAN NEWSPRINT LIMITED 
 
4266. SHRI ANTO ANTONY: 
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES भारी उद्योग मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Hindustan Newsprint Limited (HNL)  has been handed over to the State  
Government of Kerala; 
 
(b) if so, the details including terms and conditions for the same; 
 
(c) whether the Union Government has any role in functioning of HNL; 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) whether the Government has given any financial  support for the revival of this unit 
and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI KRISHAN PAL GURJAR) 
 
(a) & (b): National Company  Law Tribunal ( NCLT), Kochi, in the hearing held on 
29.01.2021 approved the resolution plan for Hindustan Newsprint Limited (HNL) submitted 
by the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KINFRA).  The approved 
resolution plan envisages th e business plan to acquire HNL as a going concern entailing a 
proposed outlay of Rs. 145,60.17 lakhs. 
 
(c): No, after the initiation of liquidation proceeding the Government of India has no role 
in the functioning of HNL.   
 
(d): Question does not arise. 
 
(e): No, the Government has not given any financial support for revival of HNL.

CONSTRUCTION OF ROADS ON BOTH SIDES OF RAILWAY CROSSINGS 
 
4267.  SHRI DULAL CHAND GOSWAMI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there is any proposal to construct roads on both sides of railway crossing 
located near villages under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY); 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)  if not, the steps taken by the Government to approve the proposal keeping in view the 
rural development? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (c)  Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched with the 
objective to improve rural connectivity to provide access to economic and social services to 
the rural population. On a road alignment selected for construction/ up -gradation under 
PMGSY, the road work including its approaches on both sid es of railway crossings falling on 
such alignment are constructed under PMGSY.

MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES   
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.4268  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.03.2022 
 
INSTITUTIONS FOR PwDs 
 
4268.  SHRIMATI SHARDABEN ANILBHAI PATEL: 
SHRI MITESH RAMESHBHAI PATEL (BAKABHAI): 
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of institutions established by the Government for the convenience of the Persons 
with Disabilities (PwDs) during the last three years in the country including Gujarat; and 
 
(b) the details of benefits to be availed by PwDs from these institutions? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF  STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SUSHRI PRATIMA BHOUMIK) 
 
(a) There are nine National Institutes (NIs) working under the Department of Empowerment of 
Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) (Divyangjan), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 21 
Composite Regional Centres for Skill Development, Rehabilitation & Empowerment of Persons with 
Disabilities (CRC) have been approved/ set up as outreach/extension centres of these National 
Institutes. Following NIs and CRCs have been set up during the last three years i.e. on or after 
01st April 2018. 
  
(i) National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation (NIMHR), Sehore, Madhya Pradesh 
(ii) CRC, Ranchi, Jharkhand 
(iii) CRC, Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh 
(iv) CRC, Gangtok, Sikkim 
(v) CRC, Balangir, Odisha 
(vi) CRC, Port Blair, Andaman & Nicobar 
(vii) CRC, Imphal, Manipur 
 
(b) The benefits derived by the PwDs from these institutions are as under:  
i. Rehabilitation services; 
ii. Provision of aids and assistive devices; 
iii. Skill Development; 
iv. Capacity development in the field of rehabilitation of persons with disabilities; and 
v. Research on disability related matters.

Chennai/Nagai/Cuddalore which are very often affected due to heavy  
rains/floods/cyclones and natural calamities every year  causing heavy loss 
to human lives/animals and properties; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c): The primary responsibility of disaster management rests with the 
State Government concerned. The Central Government, wherever required, 
supplements the efforts of the State Governments by providing logistic and 
financial support in cases of natural disasters of severe nature.  
The Disaster Management Act (DM Act), 2005 lays down institutional and 
coordination mechanisms for effective and timely management of disaster 
or impending disaster situation. As mandated by the DM Act,  the 
Government of India has established   the National Disaster Management  
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 4270 FOR 29.03.2022 
 
Authority (NDMA) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) at the 
national level. Similarly, State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) and 
District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) have been established at 
the State and District level respectively, including in the State of Tamil 
Nadu.  
The NDMA is lo cated in New Delhi and has the responsibility for laying 
down the policies, plans and guidelines for disaster management for 
ensuring timely and effective response to disaster.  One Battalion of NDRF 
is permanently stationed at Arakkonam, Ranipet district in Tamil Nadu. In 
addition, one Regional Response Centre (RRC) having a team of NDRF is 
also located in Chennai. NDRF assists the State administration in providing 
immediate and timely response to disaster s in the State, including the 
coastal areas.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4272 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
STRENGTHENING OF SHGs 
 
4272.  SHRI MOHANBHAI KALYANJI KUNDARIYA: 
SHRI RAJESHBHAI CHUDASAMA: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has received any proposal to increase the number of Self 
Help Groups (SHGs) in the States and if so, the details and the response thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to lower the interest rate on the advances given to 
these groups and keep it at par with the interest rate charged on crop loans; 
(c)  if so,the details thereof; 
(d)  whether the Government reviews the funds for SHGs from time to time and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e)  the other steps taken by Government to strengthen the SHGs? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)  The Ministry under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY -NRLM) receives Annual Action Plans (AAPs) from States/UTs which 
includes physical targets for mobilization of rural poor women into Self Help Groups 
(SHGs). The Annual Action Plans are approved by the Empowered Committee set up in the 
Ministry under the Chairmanship of Secretary (RD) for each financial year. The ultimate aim 
of DAY -NRLM is to cover at least one woman member from each rural poor household 
(about 9-10 crore) under the fold of Self Help Groups (SHGs). All households with at least 
one deprivation as per the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) database and identified 
through the process of Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) and vetted by the respective 
Gram Sabhas, are the potential target for coverage under DAY -NRLM. In t he current 
Financial Year, up to 28 th February, 2022, against the target of 7.80 lakh SHGs, 5.43 lakh 
SHGs have been formed and cumulatively, 74.80 lakh SHGs have been formed across the 
country (except Delhi and Chandigarh) under DAY-NRLM. 
  
(b) &(c)  Under the DAY -NRLM interest subvention is already being provided on loans 
taken by women Self Help Groups from Banks.   In 250 backward districts, referred to as 
Category-I districts, all women SHGs are eligible to get bank loans up to Rs. 3.00 lakh at an 
interest rate of 7% per annum. An additional Interest Subvention of 3% per annum is 
provided to women SHGs maintaining prompt repayment, reducing the effective rate of 
interest to 4%. This part of the scheme is implemented directly by Ministry of Rural 
Development and funded entirely out of the central component under DAY -NRLM. 
  
In the remaining districts of the country referred to as Category -II districts, women SHGs 
under DAY -NRLM availing loans upto Rs. 3.00 lakh from Banks, Interest Subvention is 
given to the extent of the difference between Bank’s lending rate and 7% subject to the 

maximum ceiling of 5.50% per annum. This part of the scheme is implemented by 
respective State Governments and is funded out of the allocation provided to each State 
under DAY-NRLM which includes State share as per norms.  
  
The Government has now approved an uniform interest subvention scheme for women 
SHGs across all districts in the country from next year i.e. 2022 -23. Under the uniform 
interest subvention scheme, women SHGs will be eligible for loans upto Rs 3 lakhs at 
interest rate of 7% per an num. Further women SHGs can avail loans above Rs 3 lakhs and 
upto Rs 5 lakhs at interest rate equivalent 1 -year MCLR ( Marginal Cost of Funds based 
Lending Rate) of respective lending banks. As on Mar 2022, 1 year MCLR of major Public 
Sector Banks ranges be tween 7% to 7.5%.    
   
(d)  DAY-NRLM has a provision for providing Revolving Fund (RF) at the rate of 
Rs.10,000-15,000 per SHG and Community Investment Support Fund (CISF) to the extent 
of Rs. 2,50,000 per SHG. These funds remain with the SHGs and their fe derations in 
perpetuity and are utilized to provide loans to their members to undertake socio -economic 
activities as per their micro -credit/investment plans. As on 28 th February, 2022, a total of 
Rs. 17,342 crore of Capitalization Support (Revolving Funds and Community Investment 
Support Funds) has been provided to SHGs and their federations by the Mission.  
  
(e)  The Government is taking regular steps to strengthen the SHGs by promoting SHG 
federations such as Village Organisations (VOs) and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs) which 
provides handholding support. SHGs have been provided Revolving Fund and Community 
Investment Support Fund towards credit support and to leverage high doses of credits from 
banks. Regular training programmes have been conducted for  the SHG members on SHG 
management, financial literacy, livelihoods related technologies etc.

Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a) the list of various Central Sector/Centrally  Sponsored Schemes under which central funds are  
released by the Government; 
 
(b) the objectives, annual budget, contribution share of States, eligibility of beneficiaries under such 
schemes; 
 
(c) whether any study has been undertaken or proposed to assess the impact of above schemes and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the financial assistance provided to th e State of Tamil Nadu, district-wise during each of the last 
three years, scheme-wise; and 
 
(e)  the status of major or mega fishing harbor proposed in Tamil Nadu, funds sanctioned, released,  
utilised and likely date of its completion ? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been 
implementing various schemes/programmes for  sustainable development of fisheries  and aquaculture 
in the country and the schemes implemented are as below- 
(i) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)” with  highest ever estimated investment of 
₹20050 crore with a Central share of Rs. 9407 crores, State share of Rs . 4880 crores and Beneficiaries 
contribution of Rs. 5763 crores ,for a period of 5 years with effect from the financial year 2020 -21 to 
FY 2024-25 in all States/Union Territories, 
(ii)Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)  with a total  funds size of Rs 
7522.48 crore for providing concessional finance for creation of fisheries infrastructure. 
(iii) Extension of “Kisan Credit Card (KCC)” facility to fishers and fish farmers, in the year 2018-19 to 
help them to meet their working capital needs for pisciculture.  
(b): PMMSY is implemented with the objectives  (i) to harness the fisheries potential in a sustainable, 
responsible, inclusive and equitable manner , (ii) enhancing the fish production and productivity , (iii) 
modernizing and strengthening of value chain - post-harvest management and quality improvement , 
(iv) doubling fishers and fish farmers’ incomes a nd generation of employment, and (v) enhancing 
contribution to Agriculture GVA and exports . While FIDF aims to (i) create infrastructure in fisheries, 
(ii) reduce post-harvest losses and improve domestic marketing facilities , (iii) to bridge the resource 
gap and facilitate completion of ongoing infrastructure projects . PMMSY is implemented with effect 
from the financial year 2020 -21 and the budget allocation of Rs. 700 crore was made during 2020 -21 
and Rs. 1200 crore during 2021 -22. FIDF being an interest subvention scheme, a budgetary provision 
of Rs. 10 crore each during the previous and current financial year has been made. 
  

 
The intended beneficiary of PMMSY are : Fishers, Fish farmers, Fish workers and Fish vendors, 
Fisheries Development corporations, Self Help Groups (SHGs)/ Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) in 
fisheries sector, Fisheries cooperatives, Fisheries Federations, Entr epreneurs and private firms, Fish 
Farmers Producer Organisations/ Companies (FFPOs/ Cs), SCs/ STs/ Women/ Differently abled 
persons, State Governments/ UTs and their entities including State Fisheries Development Boards 
(SFDB), Central Government and its e ntities.  Further, the intended beneficiaries  of FIDF are State 
Government/ Union Territories (UTs) and their entities including Private Sector.  
  
(c): Since PMMSY has been introduced in the year 2020 -21, it is premature to undertake its impact 
assessment study within short span of its implementation . Further, no impact assessment study has 
been undertaken for FIDF,as its implementation period has not ended. 
(d): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during the 
past three financial years, 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21, has accorded approval to the proposal worth

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4278 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
DISPARITY IN WAGES UNDER MGNREGS 
 
4278.  SHRI SANJAY KAKA PATIL: 
SHRI NANDIGAM SURESH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken steps to address the disparity in wages under 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) 
urgently to bring about equality as per clause (d) of Article 3 9 of the Constitution in 
all States/UTs; 
(b)  whether the Government has taken any steps to create easy mechanisms of ex -gratia 
payment of a fixed compensation amount for the MGNREGS workers to have a 
prompt and urgent redressal to accidental claims; 
(c)  whether the Government has any plans to provide wage support to the Adivasi 
farmers after its recent decision to disallow coffee plantation works under 
MGNREGS in the tribal areas of Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)    As per Section 6 (1) of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGA), 2005, the Central Government  may by notification specify the 
wage rate for unskilled work for its beneficiaries. Accordingly, the Ministry of Rural 
Development notifies Mahatma Gandhi NREGA wage rate for every financial year for 
States/UTs. To compensate the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA work ers against inflation, the 
Ministry of Rural Development revises the wage rate every year based on change in 
Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labour (CPI -AL). If the calculated wage rate of any 
State is coming lower than the wage rate of previous fina ncial year, it is being protected by 
maintaining the previous financial year wage rate. The revised wage rate is made applicable 
from 1 st April of each financial year. However, State Governments can provide wage over 
and above the wage rate notified by the  Central Government under Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS). 
(b)   As per the provision of the Act, “If a person employed under the Scheme meets with 
death or becomes permanently disabled by accident arising o ut of and in the course of 
employment, he or his legal heirs, as the case may be, shall be paid by the implementing 
agency an ex -gratia as per entitlement under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima 
Yojana or as may be notified by the Central Government.” 
   
(c)&(d)  Mahatma Gandhi NREGS is a demand driven wage employment programme which 
provide for the enhancement of livelihood security of the households in rural areas of the 
country by providing at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in ever y 
financial year to every household of rural area whose adult members volunteer to do 
unskilled manual work.   

  
 
Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, individual assets can be created on the own lands in which 
such households can also work and will be entitled to g et wages also as per the notified wage 
rate of the States/UTs. The works that are permissible for such farmers on their own land are: 
land development, farm pond, dug wells, other water harvesting structures, horticulture, 
sericulture, plantation, farm for estry, PMAY-G houses (unskilled wage component of 90 -95 
days), cattle shed, goat shed, poultry shed, piggery shed, fodder trough, fish drying yards etc. 
  
As per Para 5 of Schedule I of Mahatma Gandhi NREGA ,works creating individual assets 
shall be prioritized on land or homestead owned by households belonging to the: 
i. Scheduled Castes 
ii. Scheduled Tribes 
iii. Nomadic tribes 
iv. de-notified  tribes 
v. other families below the poverty line 
vi. women-headed households 
vii. physically handicapped headed households 
viii. beneficiaries of land reforms 
ix. the beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awass Yojana- Gramin 
x. beneficiaries under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers 
(Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007), and after exhausting the eligible 
beneficiaries under the above categories, on lands of the small or marginal farmers as 
defined in the Agriculture Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008 subject to the 
condition that such households shall have a job card with at least one member willing to 
work on the project undertaken on their land or homestead.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4280 
  ANSWERED ON 29/03/2022 
 
MONITORING OF CONSTRUCTION OF RURAL ROADS 
 
4280.  SHRI B.B.PATIL: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to ensure effective and strict monitoring of the 
construction of rural roads in the country and if so, the details thereof; and 
(b)  whether the Government also proposes to enquire into the global norms in utilization 
of technology in the construction of roads and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
a)    The progress of implementation of rural roads under PMGSY is regularly monitored 
by way of Regional Review Meetings (RRMs), Performance Review Committee (PRC) 
Meetings, Pre-Empowered/Empowered Committee Meetings with the States/UTs. At District 
level, the District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee (DISHA) headed by 
Hon’ble Member of Parliament (LS) monitors the implementation of various schemes of 
Government of India including PMGSY. In addition to this, special review meetings/ 
monthly review meetings are also held by Secretary/ Additional Secretary/  Joint Secretary, 
Ministry of Rural Development with Chief Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of the States/ 
UTs. 
b)    PMGSY works are executed by adopting specifications/ guidelines issued by Ministry 
of Rural Development (MoRD) and Indian Roads Congress (IRC).  
These specifications/ guidelines issued by IRC are also informed by global standards and 
technologies and IRC takes these into account in formulating its codes. IRC has formulated 
various guidelines for use of mainstream and accredited technologies.            
State Governments have been requested to propose minimum 10% of total length of annual 
proposals under mainstream technologies such as cement stabilization, lime stabilization, 
cold mix, waste plastics, cell filled concrete, paneled cement con crete pavement, fly ash etc. 
and 5% of total length of annual proposals using IRC accredited technologies such as coir, 
jute geo textiles, commercial stabilizers etc. Adoption of new technology in rural roads is a 
continuous process and regular interaction s and webinars are organized to orient various 
stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 4281 
ANSWERED ON  29TH MARCH, 2022 
  
PROMOTION OF AGRO AND FOOD PROCESSING BUSINESS IN ASSAM  
 
4281. SHRI PALLAB LOCHAN DAS: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the initiatives taken by the Government for the promotion of Agro and Food Processing 
Business in Assam; 
 
(b) whether the Government has taken several initiatives for backward and forward linkages for 
perishable agriculture products assuring quality and food safety and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the total number of food processing industries in Assam; and 
 
(d) the number of Mega Food Parks, Integrated Cold Chain and other Value Addition 
Infrastructure in Assam? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES   
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
 
 (a) & (b): Ministry of Food Processing Industries has been implementing a Central Sector Scheme- 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) since 2016-17 to achieve overall development of 
food processing sector in the country including Assam. The scheme aims to incentivize investment 
in creation of capacity in preservation and processing infrastructure thereby creating effective 
linkages of farmers with processors and markets, creating effective supply chain for perishable 
products, augmenting value chain of different perishables, promoting R&D and quality assurance.  
  
Ministry is also implementing a Central Sponsored Scheme - ‘Pradhan Mantri Formalization 
of Micro Food Processing Enterprises’ (PMFME), in partnership with the State/ UT Governments, 
under Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan with the aim to enhance the competitiveness of existing 
individual micro -enterprises in the unorganized s egment of the food processing industry and 
promote formalization of the sector.  
  
Further, a Central Sector Scheme, namely “Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food 
Processing Industry (PLISFPI)” has been launched by the Ministry in the country to support creation 
of global food manufacturing champions commensurate with India’s natural resource endowment 
and support Indian brands of food products in the international markets.   
  
(c): As per Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) data for 2018 -19, the total number of food 
processing industries in Assam were 1569 in registered sector, and as per National Sample Survey 
(NSS) 2015-16 report, there were 65,997 number of enterprises in unregistered sector in the state of 
Assam. 
  
(d): One (1) Mega Food Park, six ( 6) Agro Processing Clusters, two (2) Integrated Cold Chain 
projects, eighteen (18) food processing units, one (1) Backward and Forward Linkages project and 
six (6) Food Testing Laboratories have been sanctioned by the Ministry in the state of Assam.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 4282 
 ANSWERED ON  29TH MARCH, 2022 
  
DEMAND OF MAKHANA PRODUCTS 
  
4282. SHRI G.M. SIDDESHWAR: 
 
  Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of the rising demand for Makhana products locally and globally 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of import and export of Makhana products during the last three years, nation-wise; 
(c) the details of the expected growth in the market size of Makhana products; 
(d)  the steps taken being taken to promote Makhana products and the details of funds allocated; 
(e)  the details of collaborations with foreign countries to bring better technological expertis e in 
production of Makhana products into the country and 
(f) the details of the names of the companies producing Makhana products, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c): As per the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), 
the demand for value added products of Makhana is increasing and is expected to grow by 10-20% due to its 
nutritional value. There is no separate Harmonised System (HS) code for  exports or imports in Makhana or 
its products. Hence, estimates for the exports and imports of Makhana products are not available. Globally, 
the Makhana products are highly popular in countries such as India, China, Japan, and Thailand. 
  
(d) & (e):  Steps taken to promote Makhana products are as under: 
 
(i) The Ministry of Food Processing Industries(MoFPI) is implementing the Prime Minister Formalisation of 
Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM -FME) scheme for providing financial, technical and business 
support for upgradation/ setting up of micro food enter prises across the country. The scheme is being 
implemented on a One District One Product (ODOP) basis. Six districts of Bihar, namely Araria, Darbhanga, 
Katihar, Madhubani, Saharsa, and Supaul have been identified/ approved for ODOP for Makhana. 
(ii) As per Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with MoFPI, National Agricultural Cooperative 
Marketing Federation of India (NAFED) has incubated a brand named, 'Makhana King' to promote makhana 
sourced from various districts in Bihar. NAFED has on boarded  7 micro food processing enterprises under 
the brand 'Makhana King' and imparted training to 24 potential beneficiaries till date. 
(iii) APEDA organizes buyer seller meet for export promotion of Health products and Nutri cereals including 
Makhana.  
(iv) The regional research station on Makhana at Darbhanga, Bihar under the Indian Council of Agriculture 
Research (ICAR)-Research Complex for Eastern Region (RCER) has developed and released the first ever 
variety of Makhana, i.e., " Swarna Vaidehi " to improve  Makhana productivity. It has also developed the 
technology to cultivate Makhana in cropping system mode and Makhana based Integrated Farming System. 
   
(f): Major companies producing Makhana products, state-wise is Annexed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4285 
ANSWERED ON 29.03.2022 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
 
4285. SHRI HEMANT SRIRAM PATIL: 
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES भारी उद्योग मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of various schemes launched for the  development of heavy industries in the 
State of Maharashtra during the last three years, district-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to start new  schemes in Maharashtra in near future 
and if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
 
(c) the amount of funds sanctioned for Maharashtra  for the development of heavy 
industries in the budgetary allocation for the year 2022-23? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI KRISHAN PAL GURJAR) 
 
(a): In order to encourage investment in technology upgradation, skill development and 
augmentation of modern manufacturing capacities in the Capital Goods sector, Ministry of 
Heavy Industries notified an all -India Scheme for “En hancement of Competitiveness in the 
Indian Capital Goods Sector” (CG Scheme) in the year 2014.  The details of projects 
sanctioned under the scheme in Maharashtra are as follows: 
(i) C4i4 - Pune: A common engineering facility center named SAMARTH Udyog cen tre 
for Industry 4.0 has been established by Samarth Udyog Technology Forum (SUTF) in Pune 
district of Maharashtra, in order to demonstrate Industry  4.0 solutions to enable the industries 
to adopt the same and improve their productivity.  
(ii) Technovuus by ARAI, Pune: (https://technovuus.araiindia.com) -  TechNovuus is a 
Technology innovation platform established by Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI) in the Pune district of Maharashtra.  It encourages industries to seek solutions for 
their t echnological problems from subject experts, scientists, students and researchers at an 
online platform.  Presently it has 11,600 registered users.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED  QUESTION No. 4287 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29thMARCH 2022 
 
PROTECTION OF INDIGENOUS BREEDS OF COWS 
 
4287. SHRI HEMANT TUKARAM GODSE:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether there are thirty -seven indigenous breeds of cows in the country at present out of 
which five best breeds, i.e., Sahiwal, Gir, Lal Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi are facing 
extinction and the number of male calves is decreasing steadily;  
(b) the details of average increase in percentage of indigenous cows and calves in the country 
during each of the last three years, breed-wise;  
(c) whether the Government is considering to establish cowshed in each village for protecting 
indigenous cows and conte mplates connecting it with the Government schemes like 
MGNREGS and other schemes formulated by the Government to protect them; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 (SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) As per ICAR -National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resource, Karnal a t present, there 
are 50 registered indigenous breeds of cattle in the country. The cattle breeds namely Sahiwal, 
Gir, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi are not facing extinction. Government of India has 
been implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission with focus on development and conservation of 
all indigenous bovine breeds including Sahiwal, Gir, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi  breed 
of cattle. With mechanisation of agriculture, utility of male bovines has been reduced and due 
to this farmers are mostly rearing female calves among all cattle and buffalo breeds  in the 
country. However, in order to meet requirement of high genetic merit bulls of these breeds 
Government of India has been implementing: (i) progeny testing for Sahiwal and Gir breed of 
cattle; (ii) pedigree selection programme for Rathi and Tharparkar breed of cattle ; (iii) IVF 
technology has been promoted for production of high genetic merit bulls of Sahiwal, Gir, Red 
Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi breed of cattle and (iv) Genomic selection has been initiated for 
selection of bulls of indigenous breeds of cattle including Gir, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and 
Rathi breed of cattle.  
 
(b) National level of information regarding livestock population is collected every 5 
years. The last livestock census was conducted in 2019 and next census is due in 2024. As per 
20th livestock census 2019, the population of indigenous breeds of cows a nd calves in the 
country is given at Annexure I.  
(c) and (d) Creating infrastruc ture for promotion of livestock  such as cattle shelter poultry 
shelter, goat shelter, piggery shelter, and fodder trough for cattle is a permissible activity  
under the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA Scheme. The Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) is 
assisting Animal Welfare Organizations those are recognized by the AWBI for feeding and 
veterinary care as well as establishment of shelter houses as per their request and availability 
of funds.

FIGHT AGAINST LWE 
 
4290. SHRI KUMBAKUDI SUDHAKARAN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government had chaired a meeting  with Chief Ministers of 
10 Naxal affected States including  Kerala to push for fresh strategy in the 
fight against the Left-Wing Extremism (LWE); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the progress of the current situation 
in the State of Kerala and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether the Government had given any funds to  the State Government 
of Kerala for fighting LWE since 2016 until 2022; 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
 
(e) the number of persons killed in the Naxal prone  areas of Kerala 
between the years 2000 and 2021, year-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (e):  
i. Union Home Minister reviewed the left-wing extremism (LWE) 
scenario and progress on the various initiatives/ schemes with 
Chief Ministers of the LWE affected States on 26.09.2021. Kerala 
was represented by Chief Secretary and other senior officers of 
the State.  

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 4290 FOR 29.03.2022 
 
ii. Satisfaction was expressed in the meeting over the consistent 
decline in violence, constriction of its geographical spread across 
the country and the coordinated efforts to address the LWE  
menace.  
iii. The incidents of LWE violence have reduced by 77% from all time 
high of 2258 in 2009 to 509 in 2021. Similarly resultant deaths 
(Civilians+ Security Forces) have reduced by 85% from all time 
high of 1005 in 2010 to 147 in 2021. The districts reporting LWE 
violence have come down from 96 in 2010 to 46 in 2021. 
iv. As regards the State of  Kerala, 03 districts of the State namely 
Malappuram, Palakkad & Wayanad were included in Security 
Related Expenditure (SRE) scheme with effect from 01.04.2018. 
Projects worth Rs. 6 crore hav e been approved for Kerala under  
the Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS). An amount of Rs.6.67 
crore has been released to Kerala under the SIS and SRE scheme 
since the inclusion of these districts in the SRE scheme in 2018.  
v. There has not been any death of  civilian or Security Force (SF) 
between 2000 and 2021. However , 08 left wing extremist cadres  
have been killed during this period. Year -wise details are given in 
the annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 4294 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29TH MARCH, 2022 
 
Loss to Fisheries Exports during Covid 
 
 
4294. SHRI ANUMULA REVANTH REDDY:           
 
        Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the estimated loss to fisheries exports (within and outside the country) from the State of 
Telangana due to Covid during the last two years;  
(b) the number of fish farmers affected in Telangana due to the Covid induced restriction; 
(c) whether the Government has started any scheme to support the sector for an early recovery; 
and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
  THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) : During the year 2020 -2021 due to flight restrictions amid Covid  pandemic, a marginal 
decrease in quantity of fish exported from India has been reported by Gover nment of Telangana. 
Further, Government of Telangana also reported that there was no loss reported by fishers/ fish 
farmers, due to non-supply of fish within the country. 
(b): As reported by the Government of Telangana, no fish farmer was affected due to covid 
induced restrictions in Telangana. 
(c) & (d):  The Government of India immediately intervened to mitigate the impact of COVID -19 
crisis by announcing a number of immediate relief measures  to facilitate uninterrupted supply of 
inputs like seed and feed to the sector and to promote export s. In order to mitigate hardship faced 
by fishers, fish farmers, and fish traders, Government of India permitted unhind ered operations of 
the fishing and aquaculture industry including feeding, maintenance & harvesting in the farm, 
processing, packaging, cold chain, sale and marketing, hatcheries, feed plants, commercial 
aquaria and movement of inputs, fish/shrimp, fish pr oducts and workers. Besides, the Ministry of 
Home Affairs’ Guidelines dated 10 th April, 2020 also allowed operations of the fishing  
(marine)/aquaculture industry including feeding & maintenance, harvesting, processing, 
packaging, cold chain, sale and marketing, hatcheries,  feed  plants,  commercial  aquaria,  
movement  of  fish/shrimp  and  fish  products, seed/feed and workers. In addition, the 
Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal  Husbandry & Dairying has launched a 
flagship scheme namely Pradhan Mantri Matsya SampadaYojana (PMMSY) as a part of Atma 
Nirbhar Bharat Package with an estimated investment of Rs. 20,050 crores for implementation in 
all States/Union Territories over a period of 5 years from Financial Year  (FY) 2020-21 to 20 24-
25. All the efforts of Government have resulted in the mitigation of the impact of Covid pandemic 
on fisheries sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4295 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 29TH MARCH, 2022/ CHAITRA 08, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
WHATSAPP CONVERSATIONS 
 
4295. SHRI RITESH PANDEY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether national or international agencies are  authorised to monitor and 
decrypt any digital information  including Whatsapp conversations and if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether any guidelines have been/are being  issued by the Government to 
these national or  international agencies in order to protect citizens’  
constitutionally guaranteed right to privacy and to  prevent abuse of power 
during the exercise of intelligence gathering; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY KUMAR MISHRA) 
 
(a) to (c):  Only authorized law enforcement agencies in the country,  are 
empowered to intercept, monitor or decrypt or cause to be intercepted or 
monitored or decrypted, any information generated, transmitted, received or 
stored in any computer resource as per legal provisions of section 69 of the 
Information Technology Act, 2000. The safeguards and review mechanism 
have also been prescribed in the Information Technology (Procedure and 
Safeguards for Interception, Monitoring and Decryption of Information) Rules, 
2009, and the Standard Operating Procedure issued for the purpose.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4301 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29TH MARCH, 2022 
 
Fish Farmers Producer Organisatins/Companies 
 
4301.  SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
 Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of Fish Farmers Producer Organizations/Companies established in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh;  
(b)  whether the Government is taking any steps to improve cold storage and export of fishery 
products especially in Northern Andhra Pradesh; and  
(c)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a): The details of the Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) envisaged for  under the 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes in various States including in the State of Andhra Pradesh are as below:- 
i. The Department of Fisheries, Government of Inida through Small Farmers Agri -Business 
Consortium (SFAC), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India 
assisted for setting up of 5 FFPOs in the States of Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and 
Uttar Pradesh on pilot basis under the erstwhile Centrally Sponsored Scheme Blue Revolution -
Integrated Development and Management of Fisheries.  These 5 Fish Farmers Producer 
Organizations including the one FFPO in Andhra Pradesh have already been registered. 
ii. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada  Yojana (PMMSY) implemented with effect from Financial 
Year 2020-21, inter-alia, provides financial assistance for setting up of Fish Farmers Producer 
Organizations (FFPOs) to economically empower the fishers and fish farmers and enhance their 
bargaining power. The Department of Fisheries so far has accorded approval for setting up of a 
total of 92 Nos FFPOs during the financial year 2020-21 comprising 70 FFPOs through National 
Cooperative Development Corporation  (NCDC) and 22 FFPOs through National Fisheries 
Development Board (NFDB)  and out of these   NCDC has allocated  5 Nos FFPOs for Andhra 
Pradesh. 
iii. The Department of Fisheries, Government of Andhra Pradesh  has reported initiation of a 
program for establishment of of 50 FFPOs with financial assistance under Rashtriya Krishi 
Vikas Yojana (RKVY). 
 
(b) and (c): PMMSY, inter-alia, envisages to address the critical gap in the fish  production, 
productivity, value chain and exports . Under the PMMSY scheme, t he Department of Fisheries , 
Government of India has approved the proposals of various States/ UTs to the tune of Rs. 189 .64 crore 
with central share of Rs. 60.86 crore for development of cold chain facilities including 240 nos 
processing plants, cold storages, ice plants,  etc.  The Government of Andhra Pradesh has reported that 
establishment of 10 nos processing with cold storage plants have been selected for the State including 2 
nos in Northern Andhra Pradesh with unit cost of Rs. 40.00 crore each.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

UNREGISTERED FOOD PROCESSING UNITS 
  
4303. SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR BELLANA:  
SHRI T.R.V.S. RAMESH: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (FME) Scheme; 
  
(b) the details of the funding received by Tamil Nadu in 2020-21 and 2021-22; 
  
(c) the details of the targets achieved under the scheme in Tamil Nadu in 2020-21 and 2021-22; 
  
(d) whether it is true that there are nearly 25 lakh unregistered food processing units in the  
country and out of it more than 1.5 lakh such units are in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details 
thereof;  
  
(e) the efforts being made by the Government to register and provide them financial, technical  
and other assistance through PMFME, PMKSY etc.; 
 
(f) whether the National Portal for the FME scheme is fully functional and running; 
 
(g) if so, the details of the numbe r of new registrants of the scheme from the National Portal  
from each district of Tamil Nadu; and 
  
(h) whether any new survey has been done on the number of unregistered food processing units 
since last one which was done in 2015-16 and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
  
(a): As part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Initiative, Ministry of Food Processing Industries is 
implementing a Centrally Sponsored "PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises 
(PMFME) Scheme" for providing financial, technical and business support for upgradation of micro 
food processing enterprises in the country. Support to upgrade existing units or setting up of new 
micro units for individuals is provided through a credit linked grants-in-aid @35% up to a maximum 
grant of Rs. 10.00 lakh. The Scheme also provides support to food processing units of SHGs/ FPOs/ 
Cooperatives for credit linked grants -in-aid @35%, Seed Capital to SHGs, Incubation Centre, 
Common Infrastructure, Marketing & Branding and Capacity Building 
  
(b): A total amount of Rs.15.32 cror es as Centre Share has been released in 2020 -21 and 2021-
22 till date to Tamil Nadu for various components under the PMFME Scheme. 
  
(c): The details of achievement under the scheme in Tamil Nadu during 2020-21 and 2021-22 till 
date are as under: 
   

(i). State Nodal Agencies (SNAs), State Level Approval Committees (SLACs) and District Level 
Committees (DLCs) have been constituted.  
  
(ii). One District One Products (ODOPs) for all the 37 Districts have been approved in State. 
   
(iii). Seed Capital amounting to Rs.0.79 crore released for 281 Self Help Group (SHG) Members.  
  
(iv). 4 Incubation Centers have been approved with an outlay of Rs.8.78 crore. 
  
(v). For capacity building, one  State Level Technical Institute (SLTI) has been nominated. 26 
Master Trainers and 15 District Level Trainers have been trained. 33 District Resource Persons 
(DRPs) have been appointed to provide hand holding support to beneficiaries.   
  
(vi). Loan sanctioned to 188 beneficiaries under the scheme.  
  
(d): As per the Annual Survey of Industries, 2015-16 and 73rd  Round Survey of National Sample 
Survey Organisation (NSSO), there are about 25 lakh unregistered/ unincorporated food processing 
enterprises in the country including Andhra Pradesh. The details of Statewise number of 
unregistered/unincorporated enterprises in the country are at Annexure-I.  
  
(e): Support is being provided under the PMFME scheme to upgrade existing units or setting up 
of new micro units for individuals  through  credit linked grant-in-aid @35% up to a maximum grant 
of Rs. 10.00 lakh. The Scheme also provides support  to food processing units of SHGs/ FPOs/ 
Cooperatives for credit linked grants -in-aid @3 5%, Seed Capital to SHGs, Incubation Centre, 
Common Infrastructure, Marketing & Branding and Capacity Building.   
The Ministry has also been implementing Central Sector Umbrella Scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) for overall growth and de velopment of food processing sector, 
including processing of agro- products and thus increasing the income of the farmers. The Ministry  
provides financial support to entrepreneurs for setting up of food processing / preservation industries. 
  
(f): National Portal for the PMFME scheme is functional and running for submission of 
applications by the interested Individuals and Groups for seeking support under the scheme. 
  
(g): The district-wise details of the number of new registrants for establishing individual micro 
food processing units registered under the scheme in the State of Tamil Nadu are at Annexure-II. 
   
(h): No new survey has been done on the number of unregistered food processing units by the 
Ministry. Data related to unregistered sector is collected, compiled and maintained by Ministry of 
Statistics and Programme Implementation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 4304 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29TH MARCH 2022 
 
EXPANDING EXISTING COOPERATIVES AS MULTI-STATE COOPERATIVES 
 
4304: SHRI ANNASAHEB SHANKAR JOLLE: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION सहकारिता मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is inclined to facilitate the expansion of cooperatives as 
multi-State cooperatives as the major reasons for establishment of the Ministry of 
cooperation was to streamline the processes for ease of doing business for 
cooperatives and enable development of Multi -State cooperatives, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has found a need to recognize and categorize the 
societies that have/had real impact on the society in terms of employment 
generation, financial independence of their members, women empowerment and a 
host of other noteworthy socially responsible works and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government is inclined to further facilitate and assist the established 
Multi-State coo peratives to increase their scope of areas (States) and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) whether there is a dedicated team to look into such proposals from the cooperatives 
that have impacted the lives of people especially in the rural areas and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री  (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (b) The new ministry “Ministry of Cooperation” has been created with the mandate 
of, inter-alia, realizing the vision “from cooperation to prosperity”, strengthening of 
cooperative movement and deepening its reach up to the grassroots, promotion of 
cooperative-based economic development model including the spirit of responsibility 
among its members to develop the country, creation of appropriate policy, legal and 
institutional framework, etc. 
 
         Further, t he Government has initiated various steps to formulate new schemes 
and new cooperation policy in consultation with stakeholders including var ious 

Ministries/Departments of Central Government, State Governments, Cooperative 
Federations, etc. The new policy envisages deepening cooperatives as a true people -
based movement through promotion of new cooperatives and reaching up to the 
grassroots of the country. 
 
(c) The area of operation of multi-State cooperative s ocieties is increased based on 
their request application and  as per the  provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative 
Societies Act, 2002 and rules made thereunder. 
 
(d) A separate Ministry of Cooperation has been created with the mandate as detailed 
above. Adequate number of posts have been created in the Ministry.

4306.  SHRIMATI KAVITHA MALOTHU: 
SHRI VENKATESH NETHA BORLAKUNTA: 
DR. G. RANJITH REDDY: 
SHRI PASUNOORI DAYAKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether more than 2,600 kms of roads are still to be completed in Telangana out of 
around 14,200 kms of roads sanctioned under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana 
(PMGSY-I, II, III) and Road Connectivity Project on Left Wing Extremist Area 
(RCPLWEA); 
(b)  if so, whether 450 roads are still to be completed out of the sanctioned 3,450 roads; 
(c)  if so, the time by which the pending roads are likely to be completed by the Ministry; 
(d)  whether the Government is aware that due to incessant and heavy rains, many rural 
roads have been damaged in Telangana recently; and 
(e)  if so, the financial and other assistance that the Government is going to extend to 
GoTS to carryout repairs and restore those roads? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) & (b) The State of Telangana has been sanctioned 3,453 road works of 14,230 Km under 
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) -I, II, III and Road Connectivity Project for 
Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas (RCPLWEA), against which 3,030 road works of 
11,559 Km have been constructed a nd 423 road works of 2,402 Km are under various stages 
of execution, as per the vertical-wise details given below:-

Government. The Ministry has given a deadline of September, 2022 for completion 
of PMGSY-I & II and March, 2023 for RCPLWEA.   The implementation period of PMGSY-
III is upto March, 2025.   
  
(d) & (e)   Rural roads is a state subject. As per the programme guidelines of PMGSY, 
maintenance of roads constructed under the programme is the responsibility of the State 
Governments and all road works are covered by initial five year maintenance contracts t o be 
entered into along with the construction contract, with the same contractor, as per the 
Standard Bidding Document. Maintenance funds to service the contract are required to be 
budgeted by the State Governments and placed at the disposal of the State R ural Roads 
Development Agencies (SRRDAs) in a separate maintenance account. On expiry of the 5 
year post construction maintenance, PMGSY roads are required to be placed under Zonal 
maintenance contracts consisting of 5 year maintenance including renewal as  per 
maintenance cycle, from time to time, which are also financed by the state governments.  
           There is no provision under PMGSY for special repairs and re -construction of  roads 
damaged due to incessant and heavy rains. The state may use funds for such repairs, available 
under various other provisions.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4316 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.03.2022 
 
SUPERVISION OF CENTRAL BOARD OF FILMS CERTIFICATION 
 
4316: SHRI SUNIL KUMAR MONDAL: 
 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) is supervised timely by the 
higher level authority; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether the Government has received any  complaint or report against CBFC 
during the last six years; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING; AND 
MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
(SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) is a 
statutory body setup under Section 3 of the Cinematograph Act, 
1952 that certifies films for public exhibition.  The Ministry of 
Information and Broadcasting supervises the administrative matters 
of CBFC, like appointment and service matters of senior offic ials, 
appointment of  non-officials, budget matters, etc.  and also seeks 
inputs/reports from CBFC on different matters . The Parliament 
periodically reviews the functioning of CBFC through its various 
Committees, such as, Standing Committee on Information 
Technology, Parliament Accounts Committee, etc.  
 

(c) & (d): The CBFC has a well-defined process for certifying films in 
accordance with the Cinematograph Act, 1952, the Cinematograph 
(Certification) Rules, 1983 and the Guidelines issued thereunder and 
the complaints/ representations are disposed of  in accordance with 
the provisions of the Cinematograph Act, 1952.

Sports Colleges and Universities 
 
†4321. SHRI DURGA DAS (D.D.) UIKEY: 
SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any separate scheme for the sportsground at the village level is 
under consideration of the Government and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether any separate scheme to promote sports  in colleges is under 
consideration; 
 
(c) whether the Government has any plan to establish  a separate Sports 
University or Sports College to promote  sports at international level and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government has any plan to pr omote traditional sports in 
order to give international recognition to such sports; and 
 
(e) if so, the details of the major traditional sports  of the State of Madhya 
Pradesh and the measures taken  by the Government to promote such 
sports? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
{ SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR } 
 
(a) to (c) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility of development of 
sports, including construction of  sportsgrounds at the village level , 
promotion of sports in colleges , establishme nt of Sports Universities and 
Colleges, promotion of traditional sports in order to give international 
recognition to such sports and overall development of sports rests primarily 
with the respective State/Union Territory Governments. The Union 
Government supplements their efforts  by bridging critical gaps . However, 
under the “Utilisation and creation/upgradation of sports infrastructure” 

Page 2 of 2 
component of the Khelo India Scheme, this Ministry has sanctioned 289 
sports infrastructure projects of various categori es across the country, 
including schools, colleges and universities,  on the basis of proposals 
received from the States/UTs  from time to time.  This Ministry has also 
established the National Sports University at Imphal,  Manipur, which is a 
first of its kin d university , to promote education in the areas of Sports 
Sciences, Sports Technology, Sports Coaching, besides functioning as the 
national training centre for selected sports disciplines. The National Sports 
University will cater to students from all over the country. Further, under 
the “Support to National/Regional/State Sports Academies” component of 
the Khelo India Scheme, this Ministry has accreditated 247 sports 
academies across the country. 
 
(d) and (e) The ‘Promotion of rural and indigenous/tribal g ames’ component 
of the Khelo India Scheme, is specifically dedicated to the development and 
promotion of rural and indigenous/tribal games in the country. 
Indigenous/traditional games of Mallakhamb  (major traditional sports of 
Madhya Pradesh), Kalaripayattu, Gatka, Thang -Ta, Yogasana and Silambam 
have been identified for promotion under this component.  Grants are 
sanctioned for infrastructure development, equipment support, appointment 
of coaches, training of coaches and scholarships under this Component. 
Further, scholarship to 283 medal winners of Mallakhamb, Kalaripayyattu, 
Gatka and Thang -Ta (₹ 10,000/- per month, per athlete)  have been provided 
by this Ministry , out of which 31 winners (out of 104) in the discipline of 
Mallakhamb are from Madhya Pradesh . In addition, Mallakhamb, 
Kalaripayyattu, Gatka, Thang -Ta and Yogasana have also been included in 
the forthcoming edition of Khelo India Youth Games at Panchkula, Haryana.

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
(Department of Sports)
